correctness.rationale: For an n-ary quasigroup the (n+1)-sorted incidence R has unique completion for each other n coordinates. With k<=n+2 pebbles, moving one leaves at most n+1 fixed elements, so in a chosen sort at most two distinct forced completions arise. Cases 0/1/2 have equivalent equality and relation types; for both orders >=k, the finite excluded set has at most k-1 points, hence a generic completion exists. This establishes a permanent k-pebble strategy (unrestricted quantifier depth). Distinctness formulas separate truncated orders. At width n+3 the existential intercalate formula uses four row/column values, n-2 other input coordinates, and one reused output variable, and holds for cyclic addition exactly at even orders. Independently recomputed intercalate counts C4=4, Klein4=12, C5=0, C6=9. Finite table checks supplement, not prove, the all-n pebble lemma.

The surviving general uniform every-arity FO^(n+2) classification with matching sharp n+3 failure is not logically supplied by a binary-only lemma or by n-ary algebraic reducibility. The higher-arity extension is mathematically parallel but substantial as a stated universal bound; exact historical priority qualified.
